extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of philosophy, aesthetics, and evolutionary theory (general educated audience interested in Bergson)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting Bergson's philosophical principles about life, organization, and artistic creation — how a simple, indivisible core (impetus, movement, intuition) gives rise to complex, coordinated detail. Relevant for thinking about unity, movement, and structure in creative work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicity of function vs complexity of structure
rubrics_metrics.description: “Two points are equally striking in an organ like the eye: the complexity of its structure and the simplicity of its function.” The simple, indivisible act (the function) underlies an apparently infinite complexity of parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creative works should aim for a clear, simple core (theme, action, intuition) even when surface details are many and intricate. The complexity of detail ought to represent or decompose that simple core for the perceiver, not replace it. Anti-pattern: confusing multiplicity of details with substantive unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid mechanistic assembly (manufacturing) in explanation or creation
rubrics_metrics.description: “Manufacturing is peculiar to man... To manufacture... is to work from the periphery to the centre.” Mechanism treats an object as the sum of parts assembled from the outside in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not design or interpret a work as merely the aggregation of discrete parts fitted together. Avoid explanations or creative processes that reduce the work to component pieces whose sum supposedly equals the whole. Example anti-pattern: forcing coherence by bolt-on devices that expose the construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Favor organization from centre to periphery
rubrics_metrics.description: “Organization... works from the centre to the periphery. It begins in a point... and spreads around this point by concentric waves.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin with a central intuition, movement, or focal act and let form, detail, and variation radiate outward organically. In writing: let the central gesture/voice determine subsidiary elements rather than assembling them afterward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art as projection of an indivisible intuition
rubrics_metrics.description: “It is the picture, i.e. the simple act, projected on the canvas... conceived as a simple thing, which he has wished to transport as a whole to the canvas.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to convey a unified, indivisible impression or intuition; resist treating the work as a mosaic of smaller, separable effects. The artist's task is to project that simple whole so it may be ‘decomposed’ for the perceiver without losing its unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority of movement (unity of action) over discrete positions
rubrics_metrics.description: “If I raise my hand from A to B... movement is more than the positions and than their order... there must be something else which is neither order nor position but which is essential, the mobility.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In narrative and craft emphasize continuous movement/agency (the living act, trajectory, or animating force) rather than a sequence of isolated scenes or positions. Movement (flow, momentum) can supply coherence that mere ordered points cannot. Anti-pattern: treating plot as a mere checklist of beats without an animating impulse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canalization: limit perception/detail to effective action
rubrics_metrics.description: “The vision of a living being is an effective vision, limited to objects on which the being can act: it is a vision that is canalized.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select and shape details so they serve the work's practical or emotional 'agency' — what the characters/reader can act upon or respond to. Excess detail that does not serve the work's operative aims should be canalized or pruned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materiality as negation (visible form as obstacles avoided)
rubrics_metrics.description: “The materiality of this machine does not represent a sum of means employed, but a sum of obstacles avoided: it is a negation rather than a positive reality.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret the visible elements of a work as the result of constraints overcome rather than as straightforward additive achievements. In production, let constraints shape expressive choices; in criticism, look for what the form excludes or avoids as meaningful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coördination is binary/complete at each degree — no partial fractioning
rubrics_metrics.description: “The cause... cannot produce its effect except in one piece, and completely finished... all these organs, unequal as is their complexity, necessarily present an equal coördination.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a creative impulse reaches a certain degree, its realization should present a complete, coherent coordination appropriate to that degree. Partial or haphazard coordination risks incoherence; if a work aspires to a given intensity, its components must cohere to that intensity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve divergent tendencies (allow branching and complementarity)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Life is tendency... develop in the form of a sheaf, creating, by its very growth, divergent directions... She preserves the different tendencies that have bifurcated.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow a project to generate divergent lines (subplots, varied characters, tonal shifts) that survive rather than being forcibly unified. These branches can be complementary and reused elsewhere; an author might harvest discarded possibilities for other works. Anti-pattern: forcibly collapsing all potentialities into a single flattened path.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject pure finalism and pure mechanism; seek a higher explanatory stance
rubrics_metrics.description: Both mechanism and finalism are inadequate: mechanism sees only positions; finalism posits a preconceived plan. We must get beyond both points of view and recognize movement/impetus as prior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In creating or critiquing works, avoid explanations that reduce art either to purely mechanical assembly or to a teleological master-plan. Prefer accounts that allow spontaneity, duration, and an originating impulse (movement) that yields coordinated complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original impetus as the generative principle
rubrics_metrics.description: “An original impetus of life... passing from one generation of germs to the following generation... is the fundamental cause of variations... the impetus, sustained right along the lines of evolution... is the fundamental cause of variations.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the creative source or animating impulse of a work as primary: variations, themes, and form should be understood as emanations of that single impetus. In practice, identify and protect the project's originating energy so that variants remain expressive of it.
